title: perf-bench-latency-throughput-noah-2026-03-31
content:
Notes / scratch log - latency & throughput runs
Author: Noah Garcia (quick scratchpad)
Dates: experiments 2026-03-30, analysis 2026-03-31
Purpose: compare latency and throughput tradeoffs across quantization (fp16 vs int8) and batching strategies for open-7B and open-13B style checkpoints on A100 80GB. Quick goal: identify a default config for hosted-api small models to hit p95 < 200ms for 64-token generations with reasonable token/s cost.

Environment:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (single GPU nodes), p3dn-like instance for multi-GPU later.
- Runtime: local dev build of serving-runtime commit a3f7c (profiling flags enabled)
- Model checkpoints: open-7B (base fp16), open-13B (fp16) converted to int8 via quantize-tool v0.9 (per-channel symmetric).
- KV-cache: tested both ON and OFF.
- Batch sizes tested (requests): 1, 2, 4, 8. Microbatching disabled.
- Sequence lengths: prompt 128, generation 64 (total 192) and longer run with prompt 512 + gen 64 (total 576).
- Measurement: 30 warmup requests, then 200 measured samples. Report p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) and aggregate tokens/s over measured window. GPU mem sampled via nvidia-smi every 1s.

Quick summary (top-level):
- open-7B int8 + KV-cache ON gives best cost-throughput for interactive target: p95 ~110ms (64 tok, seq=192) at batch=1, ~950 tok/s sustained.
- open-13B int8 is competitive for throughput but p95 > 200ms at batch=1 for seq=576; need batching or dedicated reserve.
- KV-cache OFF doubles latency for multi-step generation (as expected) and reduces tokens/s ~40%.
- Batch=2 improves tokens/s by ~1.9x but increases p95 by ~30-50ms; for interactive SLAs prefer batch=1 with small model or use batching with async latency hedging.

Detailed results (64-token generation, seq=192, warmups done):
| model     | quant  | batch | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/s | gpu_mem(GB) | notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|---------|---------|---------|----------|-------------|-------|
| open-7B   | fp16   | 1     | 92      | 145     | 210     | 810      | 21.4        | kv-cache ON |
| open-7B   | int8   | 1     | 68      | 112     | 170     | 950      | 12.8        | kv-cache ON, noticeably lower mem |
| open-7B   | int8   | 2     | 120     | 170     | 250     | 1800     | 12.9        | throughput ~1.9x, p95 up ~60ms |
| open-13B  | fp16   | 1     | 160     | 240     | 370     | 520      | 34.6        | seq=192 ok but tight for p95 SLA |
| open-13B  | int8   | 1     | 118     | 198     | 300     | 720      | 19.1        | int8 helps a lot, but still >200ms p95 for longer seqs\n
Longer context (prompt 512 + gen 64 = seq 576), batch=1:
- open-7B int8: p95 ~220ms, tokens/s 420, gpu_mem 13.6GB.
- open-13B int8: p95 ~360ms, tokens/s 260, gpu_mem 20.2GB.
Conclusion: if we expect many long-context single-turn requests, open-7B int8 still manageable; open-13B pushes interactive latency beyond target without batching/scale.

KV-cache experiments (open-7B int8, seq=576, batch=1):
- KV-cache ON: first-token latency higher due to bigger KV allocation, but subsequent tokens ~25-30% faster.
- KV-cache OFF: per-generation p95 increased ~40-60ms and tokens/s dropped ~35-45%. Recommendation: enable KV-cache by default for conversational workloads; provide toggle for very short single-shot prompts.

GPU utilization notes (nvidia-smi samples):
- open-7B int8: 45-60% utilization during generation (single request).
- open-13B int8: 60-80% utilization. Observed kernel stalls at tail for fp16 13B indicating potential kernel fusion mismatch; follow-up: re-run with latest kernel selector flags.

Cost/throughput back-of-envelope (tokens/s per GPU):
- open-7B int8 @ batch=1: ~950 tok/s -> target 1M tok/day needs ~19 GPUs (24h).
- open-13B int8 @ batch=1: ~720 tok/s -> ~26 GPUs. (rough)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run open-13B with latest kernel selector + cuBLAS fallback flags (PR #784) to see if p95 improves.
- Test async hedging: send to both open-7B int8 and open-13B fp16 and use first-come; measure cost delta.
- Validate tail latencies with larger sample size (1k requests) to stabilize p99.
- Try q4f16 quantization (4-bit) for open-13B to reduce mem and check perf/correctness.
- Add tracing to map kernel-level stalls -> submit to infra for scheduler hints.

Notes-to-self:
- Save raw logs to s3://redwood-perf/noah/2026-03-30/ (cpu/gpu logs + perf traces).
- Add small test harness that runs 3 configs in parallel and outputs CSV so we can plot latencies.

Small quick-graph ASCII (tokens/s vs batch for open-7B int8, seq=192):
batch: 1   2    4    8
toks/s:950 1800 3200 4800
Note: scaling is sublinear after 2 due to memory bandwidth / kernel scheduling.

Bottom-line recommendation (short):
- Default for hosted interactive: open-7B int8, KV-cache ON, batch=1 for low-latency paths.
- For throughput/batch workloads: allow batch=2-4 with autoscaler targeting 2s queue depth and hedging fallback to open-7B if p95 spikes.

End of scratch log.
